system_description.narrative_title: Democratic midterm sweep reshapes markets and geopolitical risk
system_description.narrative_summary: A pronounced Democratic 'blue wave' in the US midterms is the dominant thread: election outcomes rapidly re-priced markets, sparked sector rotations (notably weakness in AI/data-center names and strength in cyclicals/renewables) and weakened the dollar and oil on hopes of reduced policy shocks. The system is open — election results, corporate earnings and concurrent geopolitical events (notably Iran/Strait of Hormuz incidents) act as inputs; capital flows, asset-price moves, and policy signaling are the outputs; feedback loops between markets and political actors amplify short-term volatility. Near-term dynamics are driven by investor expectations about congressional control and foreign-policy risk, producing fast, visible reallocations across equities, bonds, commodities and tech investment.
system_description.scope: Immediate interaction between US midterm election outcomes, investor sentiment, sectoral asset prices (data centers/AI, energy, financials, consumer), near-term foreign-policy risk (Middle East/Strait of Hormuz), and corporate/capital-market signals (earnings, guidance, breakups).
system_description.super_system: Global political-economic system (international capital markets, geopolitics, cross-border trade and energy flows).
adjacent_subsystems: US domestic political system (Congress, presidency, legislative agenda and oversight)
Global financial markets and investor sentiment (equities, bonds, FX, risk premia)
Energy & commodities markets (oil, shipping, Middle East chokepoints)
Tech/AI infrastructure and investment ecosystem (data centers, chips, cloud providers)

variables.name: Investor sentiment
variables.description: Measures aggregate market participants' risk appetite and bullishness expressed through prices, positioning and survey indicators.

variables.name: Net capital flow to equities
variables.description: Quantifies the net rate of funds moving into or out of equity markets across all investor types.

variables.name: Sectoral reallocation rate
variables.description: Measures the speed and magnitude at which capital is rotated between industry sectors.

variables.name: Asset price volatility
variables.description: Represents realized and implied short- to medium-term variability of asset prices across markets.

variables.name: Policy uncertainty level
variables.description: Measures the market-perceived ambiguity about future fiscal, regulatory and monetary policy directions.

variables.name: Geopolitical risk level
variables.description: Captures the prevailing intensity and probability of adverse international political or security shocks affecting markets.

variables.name: Interest rate expectations
variables.description: Represents the market consensus trajectory for short- and long-term interest rates and yield curve shifts.

variables.name: Major-currency-basket strength
variables.description: Measures the aggregate value of key reserve and trading currencies against a weighted basket of peers.

variables.name: Energy commodity price level
variables.description: Tracks the prevailing price level of broad energy commodities that transmit to trade and inflation dynamics.

variables.name: Corporate earnings surprise magnitude
variables.description: Measures the distribution and size of deviations between reported corporate results and market expectations.

variables.name: High-performance compute investment momentum
variables.description: Captures the pace of capital expenditure and financing directed toward high-performance computing and data-center capacity.

variables.name: Renewable investment momentum
variables.description: Measures the rate of new capital allocation and project development in renewable energy and related infrastructure.

variables.name: Market liquidity depth
variables.description: Represents the ease and depth with which large transactions can be executed without causing large price moves.

variables.name: Credit spread level
variables.description: Measures the average risk premium demanded over risk-free rates for corporate and sovereign debt.

variables.name: Regulatory intervention probability
variables.description: Represents the market-implied likelihood of policy or regulatory actions that would materially affect sectors or market structure.

variables.name: Market-politics feedback intensity
variables.description: Measures the strength of reinforcing interactions by which market moves alter political behavior and vice versa.

catalysts.title: Fed nominee Lisa Cook hearing (panel)
catalysts.description: Deliberative hearing on Fed nominee Lisa Cook, delayed and rescheduled by a White House panel, will clarify Fed leadership and signal policy tilt.
catalysts.rationale: “White House panel delays hearing on Fed's Lisa Cook to Dec. 14” — a scheduled hearing that raises near-term policy ambiguity and market reaction.

catalysts.title: Divided Congress reduces near-term policy shocks
catalysts.description: Democratic control of Congress (media-projected sweep) creates expectation of fewer abrupt unilateral policy changes, altering market expectations and yields.
catalysts.rationale: “Markets cheer Democratic win, betting divided Washington means fewer policy shocks” — market pricing of a calmer policy environment.

catalysts.title: Middle East oil-supply recovery / de‑escalation
catalysts.description: Reports of recovering oil supplies and market hopes for a Middle East solution drive continued moves in oil markets and risk perceptions.
catalysts.rationale: “JPMorgan, HSBC say oil supplies are recovering” and oil falls as markets hope for Middle East solution.

catalysts.title: Post-midterms impeachment/investigation dynamics
catalysts.description: Midterm results and Republican infighting increase the likelihood of extended investigations or impeachment efforts, sustaining political friction and market attention.
catalysts.rationale: “Impeachments, Iran and the presidency: what’s next” and “FirstFT: Republican infighting erupts” point to prolonged political conflict.

catalysts.title: Data‑centre chill triggers sector rotation
catalysts.description: Voter backlash and the midterm result cool data‑center optimism, prompting rapid capital rotation away from AI/data‑centre bets into other sectors.
catalysts.rationale: “AI data center stocks slide, renewables rally” and “voters have put a helpful chill on the US data centre boom.”

catalysts.title: Renewables investment momentum increases
catalysts.description: Markets price potential energy policy shifts after the Democratic sweep, boosting flows and project momentum into renewables and related assets.
catalysts.rationale: “AI data‑centre stocks slide, renewables rally” and “How the Democratic sweep could change US energy policy.”

catalysts.title: Q4 earnings / guidance season
catalysts.description: Ongoing corporate reports and guidance (many earnings headlines) will drive surprises that move prices, volatility, and flows across markets.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple earnings headlines (company transcripts, beats/misses) imply high-impact earnings surprises in coming weeks.
